title: Containerizing Ruby Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of containerizing ruby applications in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply containerizing ruby applications in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to image size and security considerations and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Containerizing Ruby Applications through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding containerizing ruby applications helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Containerizing Ruby Applications helps you reason about ruby base images. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Ruby base images. Then connect it to Dependency installation. The remaining syllabus points—Runtime configuration, Image size and security considerations—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain containerizing ruby applications, identify its place in production engineering and deployment, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
